scope: Reader PageController replacement listener ownership and initial BookPageView offsets. No app build, device run, deployment or customer data changes.

findings.problem: BookPageView and AlbumReaderSinglePageView registered a callback on the original externally supplied PageController, but replacement did not move that callback. Dispose then removed it only from the latest controller. A retained old controller kept callbacks referencing the reader state, and the new controller did not drive the custom scroll/focus callback.
findings.evidence: Before the fix, controlled widget replacement left _onPageScroll on the old BookPageView controller, both _syncFocusFromSpread and _onPageScroll in ordinary reader mode, and _syncFocusFromSpread in focus mode. All three lifecycle cases failed.
findings.fix: Detach the old callback and attach the new callback once in didUpdateWidget when controller identity changes. Rebind before the focusMode early return. Preserve existing focus/request/render state.
findings.practical_scope: The main reader currently owns a stable final PageController; this is a reproduced component replacement defect, not a measured cause of ordinary main/store frame drops.

findings.problem: An unattached BookPageView controller with nonzero initialPage initialized its render offset to zero.
findings.evidence: The initialPage=3 fixture showed page 3 but supplied offset 3.0 instead of 0.0 on its first build.
findings.fix: Initialize from current controller page when attached, otherwise initialPage. On replacement keep the existing offset because Flutter Scrollable transfers its position rather than applying the new initialPage.

baseline.classification: Intentional before-fix reproduction of the four new controlled cases.

intermediate_related.classification: The expanded focus fixture initially looked for a default focus card key; static spreads use book_flip_album_page_* keys. Corrected the fixture selector; no production change was needed for this mismatch.

verification.test_resources: Free disk was rechecked before compilation (over 8 GiB at start, about 11 GiB at final probe). No other Flutter test process was observed at the prelaunch checks. Reused existing unit_test_assets with --no-test-assets. No shared/user caches were removed.
verification.external_effects: No app build/device execution, deployment, operational database access, pricing or saved-album mutation.

checked: The same State survives six controller replacements and reuse; replaced controllers have no remaining listeners or attached scroll positions.
Disposing both ordinary and focus readers leaves all three fixture controllers with no callbacks or positions.
Book offsets follow new-controller jumps and preserve the previous page even when replacement controllers have different initialPage values.
The focus reader follows six actual jumps from a replacement external spread navigator and shows the expected live inner page.
Rebinding creates no timer, post-frame job, extra cache, image decode or per-scroll collection. Same-controller updates do not add listeners.
Existing rotation, rapid selection, turn cancellation, late network preparation, hidden capture, image quality budgets and thumbnail navigation tests pass.
Only the four controller-rebind lines were added to the pre-existing single reader changes; all other reader logic is byte-identical to the before snapshot.
review.shared_workspace: Preserved all pre-existing changes. No other task was messaged, interrupted or overwritten.

next_candidates: Review main album progressive loading and queued cover/progress work on route hiding/account changes against the latest records; add a controlled regression only when new evidence appears.
Review editor material/photo picker async completion after dismissal and ownership changes, preserving the already fixed more-menu coalescing and thumbnail request sharing.
Recheck disk and active test processes before further compilation; continue serial scoped tests without deleting shared caches.

limits: No physical device FPS, peak process memory or visual profiling was measured; no numeric performance or memory-savings claim is made.
Listener cleanup is verified through tracked callbacks/scroll positions and widget behavior; no heap snapshot or whole-app leak proof is claimed.
Multiple simultaneous PageViews sharing a single PageController are outside the existing page getter contract; this fix does not add that capability.
Existing optional book atlas/image work may finish after a page is closed under its current disposal gates; those algorithms were not changed.
